chapter: World's Greatest Jazz Band and Denver
title: Trummy Young and Marshall Royal at the party
summary: He recalls Trummy Young and Marshall Royal sounding like Benny Carter.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: And you get to see the -- for instance, did you ever get to work with Trummy Young before?
Oh, sure, sure.
Where?
In New York, at a club there.
Yeah. Well, one of the times I was there, it was the first time, they thought Trummy didn't come back. And he did sound good. Fontana was there and Rosolino and Al Grey.
Al Grey. That's another trombone player there, too. He's a young guy.
Oh, I know, the boy, the white boy.
Yeah.
Yeah, yeah. We'll put a name to him in a minute. (Bill Watrous -- ed.)
Sure will, if the tape don't run out.
That's right. But, anyway, Trummy sounded pretty good, didn't he?
Oh, sure, he sounds good, looks good.
Yes, he does.
Yeah.
Very good. Well, did -- were there any particular highlights on those parties?
Like what?
Well, any particular -- for instance, one time I heard Benny Carter and Phil Paine together.
Yeah.
I don't mean Phil Paine. I mean Phil Woods.
Well, this last time, Marshall Roval was at the party. He sounded beautiful.
Yeah.
Beautiful.
Yeah.
He and Benny Carter sounded almost alike.
Oh, yes, I bet that was very good, yes.
It was beautiful.
